sources.title: Lanes Issue board
sources.finding: Issues have title, description, instructions, CLI and worktree settings. Board statuses are customizable; issue edits auto-save; label/project/worktree filtering and bulk actions exist.

sources.title: Lanes Sessions
sources.locator: Many sessions per issue; settings; history; controls
sources.finding: Multiple named PTY sessions share an issue worktree with separate transcripts, tokens/cost/runtime metrics and lifecycle state. Claude sessions resume history; users stop/steer through terminals.

sources.title: Lanes Dependencies
sources.finding: Dependencies reject cycles and skip blocked issues during queue auto-pickup. Humans can manually move blocked issues; prerequisites reaching Done unblock dependents.

sources.title: Lanes Desktop MCP
sources.locator: Enabling; Issues; Sessions; History; external trackers
sources.finding: Opt-in research-preview local SSE server lets agents create/read/edit/move issues, start/stop/resume sessions, read history/statistics/terminal output and bridge GitHub/Linear.

sources.title: Lanes Harness selection
sources.finding: Claude Code and Codex are first-class; others run as plain shell sessions. Detects installed versions and offers install/update.

sources.title: Lanes Model gateway
sources.finding: Gateway changes provider through session environment, chiefly Claude Code Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Supports Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM and token providers; Codex file config is not driven by environment mappings.

sources.title: Lanes Worktree management
sources.finding: Issue worktrees have separate branches/directories. Sibling sessions share one issue worktree. User scripts run tests; complete-and-merge commits/merges and cleans up with dirty-work warnings.

sources.title: Lanes Git changes
sources.finding: Monaco inline diff and commit history are available. Commits stage everything; no hunk staging, side-by-side diff or conflict-resolution UI. Uncommit/discard applies only to latest unpushed commit.

sources.title: Lanes GitHub integration
sources.finding: Imports external issues with source URL, refreshes title/body after overwrite warning, and supports write-back comments. PR creation uses local gh within a session; no PR MCP tool.

sources.title: Lanes Linear integration
sources.finding: Imports Linear title/body/state/URL; MCP reads/creates/comments on tickets. Projects/cycles/priority are not mapped and state mapping is not automatic.

sources.title: Lanes Settings
sources.finding: Project JSON controls quick commands, labels, CLI flags and base branch. PR opening moves issue to Review; Done may stop sessions. Folder-access checks and launch flags are documented.

sources.title: Lanes Agent loops
sources.locator: Before you start; scheduled and fan-out examples; brakes
sources.finding: External agents drive MCP to start/check sessions and advance issues. Examples use harness loop/schedules; desktop must stay running. Verification and bounded retries/time are workflow guidance.

sources.title: Lanes Collaboration
sources.finding: Remote synced workspaces document Admin/Editor permissions, workspace chat/presence and shared board. Active issues lock takeover; AI takeover starts fresh and clears terminal history. Pricing availability conflicts remain.

sources.title: Lanes Desktop overview
sources.finding: macOS Ventura+ native Intel/Apple Silicon app. Other platforms are on the roadmap. Existing CLI login/API keys are reused; code/prompts/terminal data stay local.

sources.title: Lanes pricing
sources.finding: Free forever one-user plan; Pro $19/month up to ten members. Desktop included on every plan. Remote workspaces, Slack and automations are labeled Coming soon.

sources.title: Lanes repository README
sources.finding: Desktop uses Tauri 2/React/Rust/SQLite; local issues/settings stay in SQLite. Crash reporting is on by default with Settings > User > General opt-out. License section says Proprietary, all rights reserved.

sources.title: Lanes v0.50.0
sources.finding: Released 2026-10-31 with custom statuses and a setting controlling stop-on-Done.

sources.title: Lanes Desktop Quick start
sources.locator: 1. Install; 2. Point Lanes at your code; 3. Create an issue; 4. Start a session
sources.finding: Homebrew install, Add a project, Cmd+N creates a draft Backlog issue with Instructions, then Plan or Implement starts a session.

sources.title: Lanes Labels & Filtering
sources.locator: Assigning labels; Filtering by labels; Filtering by working directory; Filtering by workflow step
sources.finding: Per-repository labels can be assigned to issues; the board filters by label, working directory and workflow step, with sort controls.

sources.title: Lanes Privacy Policy
sources.locator: 1. Information We Collect: Analytics and Telemetry Data; 4. How We Use Your Information; 5. Third-Party Services
sources.finding: Policy covering the Lanes desktop application discloses anonymous telemetry (feature-usage events, health pings, session duration, app version, OS, crash reports) via Google Analytics 4/Firebase and Sentry. It names no telemetry opt-out control.

sources.title: Lanes Desktop MCP
sources.locator: Introduction; Settings > Integrations > Lanes MCP; Sessions
sources.finding: Lanes Desktop MCP is a research preview enabled under Settings > Integrations > Lanes MCP, with one-click connection for supported agents. Its tools start Claude Code, Codex or shell sessions against issues, stop and resume them, check status across running sessions and pull session message history.

sources.title: Lanes primary client and public repository scope
sources.locator: Install; What it is; Part of Lanes; public tree
sources.finding: The official repository presents Lanes Desktop as a native macOS application. Its complete installation/client description names no browser or native phone client. The public tree contains plugin documentation, not the proprietary desktop execution core. Separate Link, Forms and Compute products are not Desktop clients.
